tldr.text: A conceptual replication study of the findings of Carney et al. found that power posing affected levels of hormones such as testosterone and cortisol, financial risk taking, and self-reported feelings of power, and found no significant effect of power posing on hormonal levels or in any of the three behavioral tasks.
